source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 1102 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1102.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 1102 was established by Ordinance No. 32519, passed by the Dallas City Council on August 23, 2023. (Ord. 32519)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1102.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 1102 is established on property located on the north side of Wheatland Road, west of University Hills Boulevard. The size of PD 1102 is approximately 9.547 acres. (Ord. 32519)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1102.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this article:

(1) ELECTRIC VEHICLE SUPPLY EQUIPMENT (EVSE) means the conductors, including the ungrounded, grounded, and equipment grounding conductors, and the electric vehicle connectors, attachment plugs, and all other fittings, devices, power outlets, or apparatus installed specifically for the purpose of transferring energy between the premises wiring and the electrical vehicle.

(2) EV CAPABLE SPACE means a parking space with the electrical panel capacity and space to support a minimum 40-ampere, 208/240-volt branch circuit for each EV parking space, and the installation of raceways, both underground and surface mounted, to support the EVSE.

(3) GENERAL MERCHANDISE OR FOOD STORE 2,500 SQUARE FEET OR LESS means a retail store with a floor area of 2,500 square feet or less for the sale of general merchandise or food. Typical general merchandise includes clothing and other apparel, equipment for hobbies and sports, gifts, flowers and household plants, dry goods, toys, furniture, antiques, books and stationery, pets, drugs, auto parts and accessories, and similar consumer goods. The term “food store” includes a grocery store, delicatessen, convenience store without drive-through, and specialty foods store.
(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 32519)

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1102.104. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 1102A: development plan. (Ord. 32519)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1102.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit 1102A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 32519)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1102.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The following uses are the only main uses permitted:

(1) Agricultural uses.

-- Crop production.

(2) Commercial and business service uses.

None permitted.

(3) Industrial uses.

None permitted.

(4) Institutional and community service uses.

-- Adult day care facility. -- Child-care facility. -- Church. -- Community service center. [SUP] -- Convalescent and nursing homes, hospice care, and related institutions. [RAR] -- Library, art gallery, or museum.

(5) Lodging uses.

None permitted.

(6) Miscellaneous uses.

-- Attached non-premise sign. [SUP] -- Carnival or circus (temporary). [By special authorization of the building official.] -- Temporary construction or sales office.

(7) Office uses.

-- Financial institution without drive-in window. -- Medical clinic or ambulatory surgical center. -- Office.

(8) Recreation uses.

-- Country club with private membership. -- Private recreation center, club, or area. -- Public park, playground, or golf course.

(9) Residential uses.

-- Handicapped group dwelling unit. [SUP required if spacing component of Section 51A-4.209(b)(3.1) is not met.] -- Multifamily. -- Retirement housing. -- Single family.

(10) Retail and personal service uses.

-- Animal shelter or clinic without outside runs. -- Business school. -- Commercial amusement (outside). [SUP] -- Dry cleaning or laundry store. -- General merchandise or food store 2,500 square feet or less. -- Nursery, garden shop, or plant sales. -- Personal service uses. -- Restaurant without drive-in or drive-through service. -- Restaurant with drive-in or drive-through service. [DIR] [See additional provisions in Section 51P-1102.115.] -- Temporary retail use. -- Theater.

(11) Transportation uses.

-- Transit passenger shelter.

(12) Utility and public service uses.

-- Electrical substation. -- Local utilities. [SUP or RAR may be required. See Section 51A- 4212(4).] -- Utility or government installation other than listed. [SUP] (Ord. 32519)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1102.107. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217. (Ord. 32519)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1102.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the MU-1 Mixed Use District apply.

(b) Height.
(1) Except as provided in this subsection, maximum structure height is 60 feet.
(2) If the northern part of the Property abuts a district zoned R, R(A), D, D(A), TH, or TH(A), the maximum structure height is 26 feet for the first 78 feet from the northern district boundary.
(3) The following structures may project a maximum of 12 feet above the maximum structure height:
(A) Elevator penthouse or bulkhead.
(B) Mechanical equipment room.
(C) Cooling tower.
(D) Tank designed to hold liquids.
(E) Ornamental cupola or dome.
(F) Skylights.
(G) Clerestory.

(H) Visual screens which surround roof mounted mechanical equipment.
(I) Chimney and vent stacks.
(J) Amateur communications tower.
(K) Parapet wall, limited to a height of four feet.
(L) Enclosed stairwell.
(c) Increased development standards. If compliant with Section 51P-1102.113, the following yard, lot, and space regulations apply to a mixed-use project with more than 200 dwelling units.

(1) Front yard. Urban form setback is not required

(2) Side and rear yard. Tower spacing is not required.

(3) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units is 425.

(4) Floor area.

(A) Residential uses. Maximum floor area is 467,000 square feet.

(B) Non-residential uses. Maximum floor area is 24,000 square feet.

(5) Height. Residential proximity slope does not apply, but a development must comply with the height limitation provided in Section 51P-1102.108(b)(2).

(6) Stories. Maximum number of stories above grade is five. (Ord. 32519)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1102.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Increased development standards. If compliant with Section 51P-1102.113, minimum parking must be provided in accordance with Division 51A-4.200 and Section 51A- 4.1107(c).

(c) General merchandise or food store 2,500 square feet or less. One space per 200 square of floor area is required.

(d) Electric vehicle charging.

(1) In general. Except as provided in this subsection, the minimum number of EV capable spaces must be provided in accordance with this article or Chapter 53, whichever is greater. The final location of the EV capable spaces may be determined at permitting.

(2) Retail parking. A minimum of two off-street parking spaces must be EV capable spaces.

(3) Residential parking. A minimum of four off-street parking spaces must be EV capable spaces. (Ord. 32519)

SEC.51P-1102.110. DESIGN STANDARDS.

(a) In general. The design standards in this section apply to new construction. Except as provided in this section, compliance with Section 51A-4.1107 is required.

(b) Parking. Except for indented parking, parking is not permitted within the first 30 feet of a street frontage.

(c) Exterior lighting.

(1) Exterior lighting sources, if used, must be oriented down and onto the property they light and generally away from adjacent residential properties.

(2) No maximum height for exterior lighting on facades.

(d) Sidewalks.

(1) A minimum six-foot unobstructed sidewalk must be provided along all street frontages.

(2) At an intersection with drive approaches, sidewalks must be constructed of materials and finish color different than that of the driveways.

(3) Sidewalks must be continuous and level across all driveways.

(e) Pedestrian amenities. A minimum of one bench, one trash receptacle, and one bicycle rack must be located along each street frontage.

(f) Detention pond. Any detention pond must also be used for retention and include a water fountain feature. A detention pond must also be surrounded by a pedestrian path loop. Fences may not be constructed between the detention pond and mixed-use structures to the south.

(g) Required screening. Screening required by Section 51A-4.602(b) must be a minimum of eight feet in height. (Ord. 32519)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1102.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 32519)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1102.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 32519)

sections.title: Development           Bonuses       For      Mixed      Income
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1102.113. DEVELOPMENT BONUSES FOR MIXED INCOME HOUSING.

Compliance with Division 51A-4.1100 is required to obtain the development bonuses in Sections 51P-1102.108 and 51P-1102.109. The development bonuses in Sections 51P-1102.108 and 51P-1102.109 apply if a minimum of five percent of the total number of units are available to households earning between 60 and 81 percent of area median family income. (Ord. 32519)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1102.114. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 32519)

sections.title: Restaurant With Drive-In Or Drive-Through
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1102.115. RESTAURANT WITH DRIVE-IN OR DRIVE-THROUGH SERVICE USE.

(a) No queueing of vehicles is permitted on public right-of-way.

(b) A patio or open space in conjunction with the use is required between the sidewalk and front building facade. This open space, at a minimum, must measure a contiguous area of 400 square feet and include a building entrance.

(c) A maximum of one restaurant with drive-in or drive-through service use is permitted in the district at any given time. (Ord. 32519)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1102.116. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 32519)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1102.117. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 32519)
